target_customer: Players who want a hosted tabletop RPG game and pay a game master per session; game masters who earn money hosting
problem: Finding a game master and a group for online D&D meant digging through Discord servers, Reddit and specialty forums.
business_model: marketplace take rate on paid game master sessions

founders.name: Spriha Tucker
prior_employers: Google (product management for developer tools on Android Things and Fuchsia, earlier API based ad products in Search Ads)
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page; education not listed.

founders.name: Nate Tucker
founders.background_notes: Named CEO and co-founder in the May 2022 seed press release; no background given there. Not listed on the YC page.

investors: Andreessen Horowitz (led by Jonathan Lai and Andrew Chen)

technical_complexity.rationale: A two sided marketplace with scheduling, listings and Stripe payments, using standard web engineering. The hard parts were supply and demand liquidity, not technology.

defensibility.rationale: Game master supply and reviews on the platform create some liquidity advantage, but game masters can also advertise on Roll20 forums, Fiverr or Discord, so off platform leakage is easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows an incumbent copying the paid game master marketplace between 2020 and 2022.

market_need_then: Early pandemic demand for online tabletop play. The seed press release states that more than 40 million people play tabletop RPGs and that almost half of new StartPlaying users had never played before.

branding.domain_note: The old domain startplayinggames.com redirects with a 301 to startplaying.games; the date of the switch was not found.

identity.visual_style: Fantasy illustration on the site, for example a castle in the middle of the ocean as the home page title
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful and welcoming; the YC description opens with sparkle emoji and a Hello

branding.community_and_virality: Game masters publish their own blog posts and profile pages on the site; no merch or press about the brand itself found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name describes the action and is easy to say, but sources show no mascot, press on the brand or merch. Growth was credited to marketplace supply of game masters, not brand pull.

outcome_analysis: StartPlaying.Games rode pandemic era demand for online tabletop play and raised a 6.5 million dollar a16z led seed in May 2022 with over 100,000 games hosted and more than 1,000 professional game masters. No later round, exit or layoff was found, so the company reads as active and small, with market size and take rate on a niche hobby as the open question.
notes: No competitor with a source dated near September 2020 was opened, so the list is empty; Roll20 forum paid listings and Fiverr freelance game masters existed but no dated source was read. Aggregators (Employbl, CB Insights) list a separate roughly 125,000 dollar early round from Y Combinator, Musha Ventures and Bill Yu, dated 2020 by CB Insights; unverified so not recorded as a round. The seed total of about 6.6 million dollars appears only on aggregators. The Spriha Tucker YC page credits Frequentish as the earlier name, but no rebrand date was found.
